featured_reviews.name: Tejas Lone
featured_reviews.review_text: From the moment I arrived, the warm hospitality and stunning sea-facing location made a lasting impression. The rooms are impeccably clean, well-appointed, and offer breathtaking views of the Worli Sea Face. The staff is courteous, attentive, and always ready to help, making the stay feel personalized and comfortable. What truly sets Sea Corner apart is its in-house restaurant—serving delicious North Indian, Mughlai, and seafood dishes that are rich in flavor and beautifully presented. I especially loved the Chicken Banjara Kebab and the fresh prawns, which were cooked to perfection. The ambiance is cozy yet elegant, ideal for both leisure and business travelers. With reasonable pricing and top-notch service, Sea Corner Hotel offers incredible value. I highly recommend it to anyone visiting Mumbai and looking for a serene, satisfying stay by the sea.

name: Maaslli Saraswat and GSB Speciality
description:
Seafood of the Saraswat's, GSB's and Malwani's.
Food is a symbol of love and sharing. And to share this love is the sole purpose of Maaslli. The Konkan natives denote fish or seafood as Maaslli. We at Maaslli believe in serving food that speaks, aroma that endures and flavours which you savour. Blending the rich flavours of the coconut and aromatic spices like Triphal, Kokum, red chillies, nutmeg, anise and curry leaves in our dishes with the methodology of imbibing the Konkan essence in every serving. The secret to mouth watering delicacies is slow cooking with traditional cooking techniques. Maaslli brings to you authentic Seafood cuisine from lost recipes of the Konkan region.

featured_reviews.review_text: I absolutely love the food here. The bombil fry is my absolute favourite — we usually end up ordering 2–3 plates just of that. featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an excellent meal at Maaslli and would highly recommend for local seafood lovers. We went for dinner a little before 8 and the place wasn't too full tho they do not have a lot of seating. The service was prompt, efficient and polite.

We ordered the paan style surmai that was wrapped in a banana leaf and roasted, the sukha bhujane prawns and the crab soup. The surmai was the most expensive at 990 but everything else was very reasonable. The crab soup was different and tasty. The prawns were also delicious. We had it with neer dosa which was not the thin kind but a little spongy and thicker which I enjoyed. Nothing was heavy or too oily or spicy. I look forward to trying other items on their menu in the future.

featured_reviews.name: Ralph Pinto
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dishes we had:
1. Crab Lollipop: 6/10
2. Thalis with Rice Bhakaris
-a. Surmai: 10/10
-b. Pomfret: 9/10
-c. Bombil: 7/10
3. Gulab Jamun: 3/10
4. Fresh Lime Soda: 8/10

Crab Lollipop wasn't great. I have had better elsewhere.
It lacked the basic crab taste and the coating too was very mild on flavor.

The thalis were awesome. The fish were very fresh and tasty that it made our day. Surmai was the best. It had the best flavor, followed by Pomfret and then the Bombil. Surmai and Pomfret were rawa fry with little masala. It was just plain batter fry for the Bombil. We make better Bombil fry at home, so yeah.
The rice bhakari tasted awesome when it was hot.
Dry Prawns/Jhinga/Javla tasted good with the bhakari.
The pomfret fish and curry was very fresh and tasty.
Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Restaurant is smaller compared to the one near kemps corner. Cleanliness was decent. No washrooms. Only a basin is available. No Queue when we arrived at 8pm. But a queue started building later on.

Group of 4. Saturday Dinner. Mid April 2026.

featured_reviews.name: Twinkle Thomas
featured_reviews.review_text:
Horrible experience. I had come here to celebrate a special occasion with my senior citizen mother.

The AC was directly hitting our faces and food, so we politely requested the staff if they could just move the AC flap slightly upwards. We were simply told, “No, we can’t do it,” and the staff member walked away. I then requested another waiter, Mr. Mohan, who was serving us. He also refused and walked away. When I tried explaining the issue, he responded arrogantly, saying that they could not inconvenience other customers for one table.

When another table became vacant, I moved there to avoid creating any issue, but we were immediately stopped and told that the table was reserved. Even after that, Mr. Mohan continued arguing with us and grumbling, despite us sitting quietly and trying to enjoy our meal. It got to a point where I had no option but to leave.

What was most shocking was that the manager was standing right there throughout this entire incident and did absolutely nothing while his waiter was openly arguing with customers and raising his voice during dinner. Not once did he step in to de-escalate the situation or address our concern.

This was not just poor service it was complete disregard for customer comfort and basic respect, especially towards a senior citizen guest. A simple request was met with arrogance, hostility, and completely unprofessional behaviour.

I would request the concerned authorities and management to please look into this matter and take appropriate action, as no customer should have to go through such an experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5 – Authentic Malvani Taste at Its Best!

Visited Malvani Klub Restaurant at Lalbaugh with my wife, and we were genuinely impressed with the food, service, and overall experience. We ordered the Bangda Thali and Prawns Thali, and both were absolutely delicious. The Prawns Fry served as a starter was perfectly spiced and crispy, while the Solkadi was refreshing and authentic.

The Bangda fry in the thali had that perfect Malvani masala flavour, and the curries were rich, aromatic, and truly reminded us of homely Maharashtrian coastal food. The prawns curry was equally flavourful, and the chapatis were soft and fresh.

Apart from the excellent food, the staff deserves a special mention — very polite, friendly, and attentive. They made the dining experience even better with their warm hospitality.

If you love Maharashtrian or Malvani cuisine, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!

featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s been a while since we’ve enjoyed an authentic Maharashtrian meal! At first glance the place makes your feel right at home, very true to its name! We had such a great meal on Sunday, we were three of us - my brother, my sister and I.
The best thing to do when you visit is let the owner suggest their specials for you to eat, we didn’t even open the menu - we tried the Chonak Fry - 10/10, we tried the Bombil fry- 12/10 ( the filling inside the Bombil blew our mind, we had the Alu Wadi with Prawns filling - 10/10!
For main course we had the Amti with Rice Bhakri and Ravas Fry ( the Ravas so incredibly fresh) the main course was 10/10 and to top it off we also tried their Prawns Bhaat / Pulav - it was so damn good! 100/10….the Sol Kadis we tasted took us back home honestly. After this meal all we needed was our bed to sleep on cause we were in a complete food coma. An absolutely outstanding meal with a very comfortable seating and ambiance! A definite must visit again and again!

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fish Curry Rice is a true celebration of coastal flavours and seafood mastery. Their seafood spread is outstanding — the surmai and pomfret are impeccably fresh, the halwa and bombil melt beautifully, and the fish fry along with the prawns curry are rich, fragrant, and deeply satisfying.

What truly stole the show were the tisrya sukka, mori masala, and kalva sukka — bold, soulful preparations that burst with authentic coastal character. The must-try list is long for a reason: prawns aluwadi, stuffed pomfret, bombil thecha fry, and chounak fry are each crafted with precision and irresistible flavour.

Their thalis deserve special praise — generous, well-balanced, and layered with flavour, offering a complete journey through coastal cuisine. A special mention to owner Sandesh Bhat — the heart and soul of FCR — who ensures taste and consistency are always bang on, and who, along with his attentive team, is always on his toes with spot-on recommendations tailored to your mood and palate.

A place where freshness meets finesse, and every plate tells a story of spice, sea, and tradition.

featured_reviews.name: KPExplorer

Sorry, will not believe food vloggers from now on.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ A Hidden Gem for Seafood Lovers!
If you are craving an authentic, soul-satisfying fish thali, Sarang is the absolute place to be.
The Food: Simply excellent. Every component of the thali—from the perfectly fried stuffed Pomfret with its crisp coating to the rich, flavorful coastal curry—tastes incredibly fresh and expertly spiced. It’s the kind of food that leaves you entirely satisfied yet already planning your next visit.
The Ambiance: The restaurant is small and cozy, but that’s exactly what gives it its charm. It has a genuinely warm, homely vibe that makes you feel instantly welcome, as if you're dining at a close friend's house.

A delightful meal at Flavors of Malvan in Prabhadevi! The food is exceptionally tasty, wholesome, and prepared in a way that feels truly home-style, yet packed with authentic coastal flavors.

The Green Chutney Surmai was outstanding, the Fish Curry with rice was comforting and flavorful, and the Koliwada Prawns were perfectly cooked and absolutely delicious. To top it all, the Kokum Soda was simply mind-blowing—refreshing, tangy, and the perfect accompaniment to the meal.

A special mention to Vinod and Navin, who were incredibly warm, welcoming, and attentive. They took the time to understand our preferences and suggested dishes that suited our tastes perfectly, making the dining experience even more enjoyable.

If you're looking for authentic Malvani cuisine that combines traditional flavors with heartfelt hospitality, this place is a must-visit!The restaurant is Flavors of Malvan.

featured_reviews.name: Sankar Kasirajan
featured_reviews.review_text:
It was my daughter's birthday eve, and after some gentle persuasion to choose Pallavi's boutique café over Mumbai stalwarts like Trishna or Mahesh, we were seated in this beautifully done-up spot near Dadar's Shivaji Park. Though small, the space possesses a premium, fine-dining ambiance.

The Feast
Despite claiming to be "light eaters" (ahem!), we indulged in a vast selection, and every single dish was amazing. The true "Flavours" of Malwan shone through, outperforming many other seafood restaurants I've visited over the past 28 years (including Gajalee, Mahesh Lunch Home, and Sindhudurg).
Our order included:
	Refreshing Drinks: Sol Kadi, Kokum Soda, and Lemon Soda.
	Signature Seafood: Chutney Stuffed Pomfret Fry with Prawns, Chutney Stuffed Bombil Roll with Prawns, Sukka Crab, Tisrya Sukka, and Prawn Curry, paired with Rice Bhakri.
	Desserts: Ukdiche Modak and Puran Poli.

The Unforgettable Star
While every item was a feast for the taste buds, the Sukka Crab was the undisputed champion—absolutely outstanding! We literally wiped the plates clean and even drank the leftover Prawn Curry. This is food made with passion; food that truly leaves a lasting memory.

My words and photos simply cannot do full justice to the culinary magic at "Flavours of Malwan."

Don't just read about it—experience the authentic, soulful taste of Malwani cuisine for yourself!

featured_reviews.name: Anvi Kaale
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently had lunch at this restaurant and it was truly a fantastic experience! Authentic malvani taste.😋 The flavors were absolutely amazing, and every dish was prepared to perfection. 💯 I highly recommend trying their delicious offerings. Will definitely be back for more! ✨👍

featured_reviews.review_text:

Overall, it’s a nice and cozy restaurant, especially for non-vegetarian lovers. 🐟🍽️

featured_reviews.name: Nitin Guddeti
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a wonderful experience at Flavours of Malvan! The Prawns pulav and Bombil Thali were absolutely delicious, packed with authentic Malvani flavors. Fresh seafood, flavorful curries, crispy fry, and refreshing solkadhi made the meal truly satisfying. Highly recommended for seafood lovers looking for an authentic taste of the coast. 🐟🦐😋

featured_reviews.name: Greeshma Gowda
featured_reviews.review_text: Walked into this restaurant when we were in Dadar on a Sunday evening. Its a small restaurant on the ground floor of a residential buidling. There was a waiting time of 30 mins to get in. We ordered the pomfret thalli and crab thalli. The service is slow but it was worth the wait. The crab was soft and well cooked and the gravy was delicious. We also had sweet lime soda and lemon ginger drink. Last we had ukdiche modak which was also tasty.

featured_reviews.name: Meghna Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything tasted like it was cooked in someone’s very talented Malvani aaji’s kitchen. The bombil fry? Illegal levels of good. The mutton sukka + the prawn thali? Had me contemplating licking the plate. The puran poli and the modaks? Felt like a hug in dessert form. Just solid recommendations from the team and great vibes all around.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Full marks overall !

featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a very popular Malavni & Kokani cuisine  restaurant  in Lalbaug area.
It is popular for its fresh seafood,Mutton & chicken dishes.
It follows thali system.
Ambiance  is simple & ethnic,comfortable seating,fully air-conditioned . There are two restaurants with different decor but same menu separated bya spectacle shop.

Their menu has a few seafood,Mutton & chicken starters.
Then different varieties  of thalis.
We had specially gone there to have good fresh seafood but found the rates too high as they were as per size.
A Surmai orpomfret thali at around 1000/- however big the fish sounds too high so we had to skip them.
We had a Prawn thali which was tasty with vade & had fried prawns not very big,prawn masala,fish curry,sol kadi,vade & rice for 550/- which was good & tasty.

On the whole it was a good meal except for the high pricing of fish items. No rice dishes like biryanis are available  on the menu which is also disappointing.
Can visit with family when in lalbaug area.

The restaurant is spacious with seating options available for all size of groups. Loved the lights done on the ceiling as it looks traditional. The hanging lamps and the perfectly placed bar looks excellent.

featured_reviews.name: Prachiti Gadekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
During a recent visit to Yazu Pan Asian Supper Kitchen in Lower Parel, I had the opportunity to indulge in a diverse and flavorful spread that truly showcased the restaurant’s mastery over Asian cuisine. From the moment we arrived, the ambiance set the tone for a relaxed yet upscale dining experience. The service was courteous and efficient, with dishes arriving promptly and plated beautifully.

Our meal began with the Prawn Tempura Roll, which was light, crispy, and paired with just the right balance of sauces. It was followed by the Sriracha Chicken that packed a punch of heat, complemented by a slightly sweet undertone. The Yazu Signature Sichuan Garlic Prawn stood out with its bold flavors and perfectly cooked prawns, a definite must-try for seafood lovers. Another highlight was the Yazu Signature Chicken, which offered a rich and savory profile that paired well with the other mains.

For noodles, the Phad Thai Noodles were enjoyable, with a classic tamarind flavor and the right mix of textures. The Chicken in Hot Garlic Sauce added a spicy, garlicky depth to the meal that was satisfying and comforting. We also tried the Shojo, which added a refreshing and slightly lighter touch to the otherwise intense flavor profile of the dishes.

To end on a sweet note, we ordered the Mathilda Cakes Pull Me Up. It was a delightful dessert that offered a decadent and fun experience, perfectly capping off our evening.

Overall, Yazu delivered a memorable culinary experience with a well-rounded menu and elegant atmosphere. It's a great choice for those looking to explore Pan Asian cuisine with a modern twist in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavin Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazu is a Pan‑Asian “supper club” concept that brings together flavors from Japan, China, Thailand, Korea and Southeast Asia under one roof. The Lower Parel outlet is positioned as a flagship. The place is spacious combining indoor and outdoor elements. The branding emphasizes “visual experiences” — sculptural ceiling installations, patterned concrete flooring, carved wooden walls, lighting as focal décor elements. Ambience is amazing: stylish, atmospheric, good for evenings, date nights, or a premium outing. The décor and lighting get special and the ceiling installation, carved walls, and an aesthetic that’s “Instagram‑worthy.” After sundown, it transforms into a high‑energy bar/music venue  like “Studio Nights”.
Wide and ambitious menu: sushi, sashimi, maki, dim sum, baos (Taiwanese street bun), Teppanyaki, Robata grill items, curries, fusion dishes (e.g. “Asian Pizza‑San”) etc. They offer special dietary menus: Jain and Keto options. Go for signature dishes (e.g. sushi rolls, baos, dim sum) early; save room for dessert.
Top Picks:
• Black crispy Asparagus Roll (sushi) • Steamed Veg. Cheung Fung • Veg. Dimsum Experience Basket (7 piece) • Spicy Lotus root • Mah Poh Tofu etc.
• For soups: the Tom Kha, Tom Yum are superb.
• Desserts are also a highlight: “Pull Me Up Tiramisu”, “Berry Blossom Cheesecake”, “Salted Caramel Tart”, Coconut Panna Cotta etc. Presentation is premium, textures and flavors seem well balanced in many reviews.
• Drinks are highly inventive, globally inspired, and expertly crafted. Every sip is bold and gives unforgettable experience. Loved its Samurai (cocktail), Shojo and Yashi (mocktails) which were flavorful and refreshing.
Attentive and polite staff who guide through the menu, make recommendations, and ensure a comfortable dining experience. Yazu Lower Parel is a strong pick if you're looking for a premium Pan‑Asian dining + bar experience in Mumbai. The ambience, décor, and overall concept are standout features. The place has a premium, elegant vibe and delivers a memorable night out.

featured_reviews.review_text:
YAZU delivers a standout lunch experience. The staff was warm, attentive, and genuinely courteous throughout, making the meal feel relaxed and welcoming.

Highlights included the cream cheese truffle dumplings (the pink ones), hands down the best bite, and the mushroom money bags, crispy with great texture and depth of flavor. The YAZU signature chicken was bold and satisfying, and the wonton soup was light, comforting, and perfectly balanced.

The affogato and cold coffee were an excellent pairing too with the spicy flavors—smooth, rich, and a perfect way to wrap up lunch. A refined yet approachable Pan-Asian spot with fantastic food, strong attention to detail, and great service. Highly recommend.

KOKO, Lower Parel – A Luxe Asian Dining Experience

KOKO in Lower Parel offers a refined and memorable dining experience. The ambiance is top-notch — modern, elegant, and perfect for an evening out. The menu features an impressive variety of sushi and dim sum, with ample vegetarian choices that are just as flavorful and thoughtfully prepared as the non-vegetarian options.

The staff is courteous and attentive, adding to the overall premium feel of the place. However, a heads-up for first-timers — they don’t usually offer tables without a reservation, even if some appear to be vacant. Be prepared to sit at the bar if you walk in without prior booking.

That said, once you’re seated, the food and experience are absolutely worth it. For anyone who appreciates quality Asian cuisine in a sophisticated setting, KOKO is highly recommended — just make sure to reserve in advance!

featured_reviews.name: Travelling Doctor
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located on the 3rd floor of Atria – The Millennium Mall, Global Fusion remains one of Mumbai’s most iconic destinations for an upscale buffet experience. It is particularly famous for its "Grandeur" theme, combining luxury interiors with a massive spread that leans heavily into Japanese, Chinese, and North Indian cuisines.
Ambiance & Vibe
From the moment you step out of the mall’s glass elevators, the restaurant impresses with its scale.
The Setting: The decor is lavish and "moody," featuring warm, golden lighting, stone-textured pillars, and a signature indoor water pond with a pagoda-style structure.
The Vibe: It strikes a balance between a high-energy dining hall and a sophisticated lounge. It is an excellent choice for celebratory group dinners or corporate team outings where you want a "wow" factor without the stiffness of formal fine dining.
The Culinary Spread: Quantity Meets Quality
The sheer variety here is arguably the best in Mumbai for Asian food lovers.
The Sushi & Sashimi Station: This is the highlight for many. Unlike standard buffets, the sushi selection is extensive, featuring everything from classic California rolls to innovative vegetarian nigiri.

The "Chit System" for Starters: One of the most appreciated features is the live starter service. Instead of picking up cold appetizers from a counter, you browse the display, select what you like, and hand a chit (token) to your waiter.
Freshness: This ensures that your prawns, dumplings, and kebabs arrive at your table piping hot and freshly prepared.
Must-Trys: The Tempura Prawns, Baked Cheese Prawns, and the Shanghai Chicken Dumplings are perennial favorites.
Main Course: While the starters usually take center stage, the mains offer a solid range of Thai curries, noodles, and even North Indian classics like Dal Makhani for those wanting a familiar comfort.
Service Dynamics
The service at Global Fusion can be a bit of a "double-edged sword."
The Effort: You will see waiters working incredibly hard, often juggling dozens of chits and running between the live kitchen and the vast seating area.
The Challenge: Because the restaurant is almost always at capacity (especially on weekends), the staff can feel stretched thin. You might experience a slight delay in your starters arriving or find it difficult to catch a server's attention during peak hours. However, their attitude is generally helpful and polite despite the high-pressure environment.
The Sweet Ending
If there is one area that feels slightly scaled back compared to the massive appetizer section, it is the desserts.
Variety: While the selection is a bit more limited, it covers the essentials well.
Quality: You can expect high-quality Baskin-Robbins ice cream, mini cheesecakes, and chocolate mousse. The taste is consistently good, even if the "theatre" of the dessert section doesn't quite match the sushi or teppanyaki counters.
Value for Money
Global Fusion is not a budget-friendly outing. With prices of approx Rs 2000 per person, it is one of the costliest buffets in the city.
The Verdict: You are paying for the variety and the premium ingredients (like prawns, crab, and sashimi) that you simply won't find at cheaper buffet chains. If you have a large appetite and a love for Asian starters, it is well worth the splurge.

For a place that claims to offer a wide variety of cuisines, the quality was shockingly poor. Nothing felt fresh and most of the dishes were barely edible.

The only thing that was remotely decent was the prawn tempura. It was crispy and actually tasted good — but one good item cannot save an entire buffet full of bad food.

The service didn’t help either. Staff seemed uninterested and the overall dining experience felt careless and poorly managed.

For the price they charge, this place is absolutely not worth it. There are far better restaurants where you can get good quality food and service.

I strongly advise people to avoid Global Fusion and spend their money somewhere else.

Special mention to Mr. Ravindra Nigudkar, who has brought the real taste of Malvan to Mumbai — you can feel the passion in every dish.
